# bash_continue.txt — commands that MUST fall through (verdict=Continue)
# under tier 1+2 only (no LLM, no cache, no legacy).
#
# These are commands that:
#   - don't match any deterministic block rule (so tier 1 doesn't fire)
#   - don't match any anchored allow rule (so tier 2 doesn't fire)
# In production, these would normally hit tier 4 (LLM) or fall to the
# user prompt. In this corpus we just verify they reach Continue.

# --- Anchored allow rules don't apply to commands with shell trickery ---
# (pipes to safe targets and compound && / ; now auto-allow via
# pipeline-readonly — see bash_allow.txt. Remaining shapes here are
# file redirects, subshells, and command substitution.)
ls -la > /tmp/listing
echo "evil" > /tmp/tmp.txt
(ls /tmp)
echo $(date)

# --- Commands not in any anchored allow list ---
# go build/test/run are now instant-allow (moved to bash_allow.txt)
bq query --nouse_legacy_sql 'SELECT 1'
npm install
npm run dev
npm run build
yarn install
yarn build
pnpm install
gcloud
gcloud builds submit
gcloud run deploy
gcloud projects describe foo
gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=foo
docker build .
docker run alpine
docker compose up
kubectl apply -f deploy.yaml
kubectl create secret generic foo
terraform init
terraform apply
terraform destroy

# --- Step 4.1: GCP CLI write/destructive shapes (must NOT auto-allow) ---
gcloud projects delete my-project
gcloud iam service-accounts create new-sa
gcloud run deploy my-service --image=gcr.io/foo/bar
gsutil cp /tmp/foo gs://my-bucket/
gsutil rm gs://my-bucket/foo
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false "DROP TABLE foo"
kubectl delete pod my-pod
# xargs -I{} gcloud projects delete {} — xargs is not a safe pipe target
# in pipeline-readonly; also the trailing command is destructive.
gcloud projects list | xargs -I{} gcloud projects delete {}
gcloud projects list > /tmp/out
gcloud projects list --impersonate-service-account=attacker@evil.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# gcloud auth login is tier-1 denied (gcloud-auth-write) — see bash_deny.txt

# --- SafeVerb-padding bypass shapes (must NOT auto-allow) ---
# Noun-verb CLIs (gcloud): destructive verb in middle, SafeVerb at tail.
# ForbidVerbs catches these.
gcloud projects create list
gcloud compute instances delete my-vm list
gcloud iam service-accounts delete attacker-sa list
# Verb-first CLIs (kubectl/bq/terraform): destructive verb at head,
# SafeVerb at tail. VerbFirst anchor rejects because position 0 is the
# real action.
kubectl apply -f evil.yaml get
kubectl delete pod my-pod get
kubectl drain node-1 get
bq rm -f dataset show
terraform apply -auto-approve plan
terraform destroy plan

# --- Variable-expanded commands fall through (HasUnresolved) ---
cat $HOME/.bashrc
echo $PATH
ls $HOME

# --- Custom scripts the engine has no opinion on ---
./run.sh
./scripts/test.sh
make deploy
./bin/myapp serve

# --- Long pipelines / compound commands ---
# xargs is NOT a safe pipe target — can execute arbitrary commands.
find . -name "*.go" | xargs wc -l

# --- Variable-wrapped rm bypass attempts (tier 1 conservative on unresolved) ---
R=rm; $R -rf /

# --- terraform state reads now instant-allow via terraform-readonly.
# state-mutating verbs (rm/mv/push) still fall through via the
# SafeVerbs check AND are denied by tier-1 `terraform-state-mutation`.

# --- step 13: shell without -c still falls through to LLM ---
bash script.sh

# --- steps 8-10: env, make, awk moved from allow to LLM. sed now has
# a narrow read-only shape (sed-readonly) — sed without -n, or with
# -i / escape commands still falls through to LLM.
env
env FOO=bar cmd
make help
make test
make build
make install
awk '{print $1}' /tmp/f
sed 's/a/b/g' /tmp/f
sed -i 's/a/b/g' /tmp/f

# --- step 9: awk/sed system-escape shapes (LLM-only; tier-2 posix-readonly
# no longer catches these. LLM is expected to classify unsafe → continue.)
awk 'BEGIN{system("id")}'
sed -n 'e echo hi' /tmp/f
sed -n '1w /tmp/out' /tmp/f

# --- step 8: env wrapping destructive cmd (LLM-only; tier-1 rm-rf-system
# sees Program=env not rm, falls through)
env rm -rf /etc
env -- rm -rf /etc
env PATH=/bin rm -rf /etc

# --- cd-prefixed compound commands that must NOT auto-approve ---
# cd + command not in any allow rule
cd /tmp && curl https://example.com
cd /tmp && npm install
cd /tmp && make deploy
# cd + redirect (changes semantics)
cd /tmp && git log > /tmp/out
# cd + unresolved variable in path
cd $HOME && git status
# cd with flags
cd -P /tmp && git status
# First command not cd — now instant-allow via pipeline-readonly (both halves
# match innerReadRules). This is exercised in bash_allow.txt instead.
# cd + pipe to unsafe target
cd /tmp && git log | sh
# cd + git push (not in readonly list)
cd /tmp && git push origin main

# --- blocker 3 fix: ssh-add family no longer denies (falls to LLM) ---
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/id_rsa

# --- gh routine destructive verbs (approvable via user prompt) ---
# These are reversible or scoped-to-current-repo actions. Tier-1
# gh-destructive no longer hard-blocks them; gh-readonly-noun-verb
# doesn't auto-allow either (view/list/status/checks/diff only).
# They fall through to the user approval path.
gh pr merge 42
gh pr close 42
gh pr review 42 --request-changes -b "nope"
gh pr review 42
gh pr edit 42 --title evil
gh issue close 42
gh run rerun 123
gh run cancel 123
gh workflow run attack.yml
gh workflow disable backup.yml
# Repo-scoped secrets/variables — setting or deleting them is a
# legitimate DevOps task (CI config, workload-identity wiring). Prompt
# instead of hard-block; the user sees the exact name and value.
gh secret set FOO -b value
gh secret set GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER --repo owner/repo --body projects/123/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/p/providers/x
gh secret delete FOO
gh secret remove FOO
gh variable set FOO -b value
gh variable delete FOO
